subject: Post-call: Model fit & safety evals + next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Emily Chen <emily.chen@healthscope.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-call: Model fit & safety evals + next steps

Hi Emily / Team,

Thanks again for the time today - great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on scope and handoffs: 

Recap:
- Goal: Evaluate candidate models for HealthScope's triage assistant (sensitive medical domain) focusing on model fit, safety/refusal behaviors, and latency at 99th percentile for patient-facing flows.
- Key constraints: strong refusal behavior on high-risk prompts, auditability for outputs, and predictable latency for peak clinic hours.

Recommended initial models to evaluate (shortlist):
- redwood-llama-70b-quant (good raw quality; needs strong guardrails)
- redwood-2b-refiner (lower cost, faster tail latency; good for templated prompts)
- open-encoder-7b (baseline for embedding + rerank experiments)

What we're sending (attached + links):
- safety-eval-report (PDF) - baseline safety/refusal scans against Redwood's rule sets
- prompt-sets.csv - suggested prompt families and edge cases to run (sensitive/medical refusal, hallucination probes, escalation triggers)
- 99p latency benchmark CSV and a short note on expected performance per config

Proposed evaluation plan / timeline:
1) HealthScope selects a 500-1,000 sample prompt set from the attached prompt families (we can help prioritize).
2) Redwood runs automated evals across the three candidate models (safety/refusal, accuracy proxies, and latency) - ~5 business days after we receive the sample set.
3) We deliver a short report and a recommended configuration (quantization + batching + guardrail prompt set) and propose a canary run with real traffic in a dedicated capacity slot.

Immediate asks for Emily / procurement:
- Can you confirm who on your side will own the sample prompt selection and procurement contact?
- Any must-have compliance artifacts (SOC2 snapshot, IP flow diagrams)? We'll loop Rafael for SOC2 packets.

Next call: I can set up a 30-min follow-up early next week to finalize the sample set and timeline. Proposed times: Tue/Wed morning PT.

Thanks - putting Rafael and Marcus on copy so they can jump in on the compliance and infra details.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: healthscope-safety-eval-report.pdf, healthscope-prompt-sets.csv, redwood-benchmark-99p-latency.csv
From: Dr. Emily Chen <emily.chen@healthscope.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, procurement@healthscope.com
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & safety evals + next steps

Hi Marissa - thanks for the clear recap. A few quick items from our side: 

- This plan looks good. We will own the sample selection; I'll pull together a prioritized set (~700 prompts) and share by EOD Monday.
- Two asks: 1) Can you confirm 99th percentile latency for the redwood-2b-refiner and the 70b quant option under a canary (dedicated) config? We need to ensure sub-800ms tail for patient-facing responses. 2) Please include the SOC2 evidence and any data handling diagrams we can pass to procurement.
- Procurement contact: procurement@healthscope.com (cc'd). They'll need an initial SOW/cost estimate and a rough timeline for a 2-week pilot.

Also interested in any early-run guardrail prompt examples you can share - we want to validate refusal behaviors for medication recommendation prompts and suicide/self-harm escalations.

Emily
Dr. Emily Chen
VP Clinical Products, HealthScope
emily.chen@healthscope.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Emily Chen <emily.chen@healthscope.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, procurement@healthscope.com
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 12:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & safety evals + next steps

Thanks Emily - really helpful. Quick answers and next steps below.

Latency / canary config:
- redwood-2b-refiner (dedicated, modest batching): typical 99p ~ 450-650ms for single-turn prompts at mean token length 40; sub-800ms is achievable with dedicated capacity and conservative batching (we'll reserve a canary pool).
- redwood-llama-70b-quant (dedicated, optimized kernels): 99p is more variable (typically 700-1,200ms depending on sequence length and KV cache behavior). For patient-facing paths we recommend the 2b-refiner as primary with the 70b quant as a higher-quality fallback for complex completions.

Compliance / SOC2 packet:
- Rafael - I've asked Rafael to attach the SOC2 snapshot and data flow diagrams to this thread. Rafael, can you confirm ETA to share the packet?

Guardrail prompts / refusal behaviors:
- Attached prompt-sets.csv contains families for medical advice refusal, escalation prompts (urgent language), hallucination probes, and sensitive extraction tests. Example guardrail: prepend a short system instruction that requires the model to refuse giving prescriptive medication guidance and instead present triage options plus a 'seek clinician' escalation.

Cost / SOW:
- For the pilot (2 weeks, canary slot, 100 req/s sustained test window) we'll put together an initial cost estimate and SOW for procurement. That will include dedicated capacity pricing, any additional observability retention, and a short line-item for evaluation engineering time. Expect a draft within 24-48 hours.

Proposed next steps:
1) Emily to share sample prompts by Monday EOD.
2) Redwood runs automated evals (5 business days) once we receive the set.
3) Canary run discussion and procurement SOW (Rafael to attach SOC2 + Marcus to confirm infra config).

I'm available Tue/Wed mornings PT - I'll send a calendar invite for Tue 9:30am PT unless you prefer a different time.

Thanks - Marissa

--
